observations.body: Skip to content PROGRAMMING ⌄ ⌑ Reserve → JAZZ LOUNGE & SUPPER CLUB • DOWNTOWN Sonic Gastronomy for nights that linger. The Midnight Note is a charcoal-dark listening room where brass glows, plates arrive on cue, and every set is paced like a tasting menu. Reserve a table for tonight’s program—or apply for membership to unlock late-night access and cellar selections. Reserve Seats → Explore Tonight’s Lineup → Doors 6:30 • First set 7:30 Chef’s Tasting (5 courses) • Limited Dress: evening casual Tonight • “Blue Hour” Trio • 9:45 set A slow-rotating brass ring echoes cymbal shimmer—our signature motif for sound in motion. Sensory Pillars Three entrances to the same night: the music, the menu, and the room itself. Tap a pillar to expand the experience.Room Atmosphere Listen Curated sets with vinyl warmth and stage intimacy. Taste Seasonal courses timed to the set list. Listening Room Protocol Our stage is mixed for clarity, not volume. Sets are framed by short intermissions—enough time to refresh a drink, not enough to break the spell. House system tuned for upright bass definition and cymbal air. Vinyl prelude from the club library before each first set. Quiet service choreography; menus land between tunes. Artist Lineup Four pillars of sound, each with its own cadence. Filter by vibe to shape your night. mobile_observations.body: Skip to content PROGRAMMING ⌄ ⌑ Reserve → JAZZ LOUNGE & SUPPER CLUB • DOWNTOWN Sonic Gastronomy for nights that linger. The Midnight Note is a charcoal-dark listening room where brass glows, plates arrive on cue, and every set is paced like a tasting menu. Reserve a table for tonight’s program—or apply for membership to unlock late-night access and cellar selections. Reserve Seats → Explore Tonight’s Lineup → Doors 6:30 • First set 7:30 Chef’s Tasting (5 courses) • Limited Dress: evening casual Tonight • “Blue Hour” Trio • 9:45 set A slow-rotating brass ring echoes cymbal shimmer—our signature motif for sound in motion. Sensory Pillars Three entrances to the same night: the music, the menu, and the room itself. Tap a pillar to expand the experience.Room Atmosphere Listen Curated sets with vinyl warmth and stage intimacy. Taste Seasonal courses timed to the set list. Listening Room Protocol Our stage is mixed for clarity, not volume. Sets are framed by short intermissions—enough time to refresh a drink, not enough to break the spell. House system tuned for upright bass definition and cymbal air. Vinyl prelude from the club library before each first set. Quiet service choreography; menus land between tunes. Artist Lineup Four pillars of sound, each with its own cadence. Filter by vibe to shape your night. Courses arrived exactly between tunes—felt composed.” MN Midnight Notes JL Jazz Ledger Amira S. The room breathes.” SR Supper Review NW Night Wire Club Records Numbers that tell a story—sets played, cocktails built, and the artists who have crossed our stage. +500 Shows performed since opening night +80 Signature cocktails in the Midnight Book +12 Grammy winners hosted for special sets Performance Archive Browse nights that shaped the room. Hover or tap an entry to reveal a photographic memory with subtle parallax. ♩ The Quartet Residency Brush drums, upright bass, close mics → ♙ Vocal Series Vintage mic nights with smoked light → ◎ Vinyl Listening Salons Curator-led sides, silent room, deep cuts → ‡ Neon Sign Sessions Late sets under glowing reds and greens → The Quartet Residency Stage intimacy • close-mic detail Four players, one room, and a hush that made every note feel inevitable. The residency defined our sound: a bass you can trace with your eyes, a ride cymbal that blooms instead of bites. Journal / Backstage Notes from the room: how we build the menu, tune the system, and program the night. Spotlight 7 min read Interview with the Musical Director On pacing a night like a record: side A for clarity, side B for heat, and an encore that feels like a secret track. Noah K. • Programming → Kitchen 5 min read Why our tasting menu lands between tunes Timing is a flavor. We design each course so the last bite resolves before the next downbeat. It’s hospitality with a metronome. Elise R. • Culinary → Room 6 min read Acoustic design: the art of soft reflections A listening room should feel intimate without becoming dry. Here’s how we shaped the ceiling and walls to keep cymbals airy and vocals present. Mina P. • Design → Membership For guests who return often: priority reservations, members-only late sets, and cellar access for special nights. Executive Chef ELISE ROWE Builds menus like arrangements—contrast, repetition, surprise. Member nights include off-menu courses and paired flights designed for specific lineups. Creative Director JONAH VALE Curates the room’s atmosphere: the glow of the bar, the pacing of the night, and the sound-wave motifs that thread through every season’s program. Applications reviewed weekly • Member access includes a dedicated concierge line. Apply for Membership → Reserve Choose your seating, your set, and whether you’d like the chef’s sequence.
